steps.body: Line things up to compare length! Start at the **same end**. The one that sticks out is **longer**.
Align the start and cover the object with equal units.

widget.prompt: Measure the ribbon. Align zero with its start, choose one-unit blocks, and place four blocks with no gaps or overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: Four equal one-unit blocks cover the ribbon exactly. Same start, no gaps, no overlaps.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the ribbon’s starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end—no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Use the one-unit block so the count tells the ribbon’s length in units.

cml.actionGoal: Measure by zero alignment and iterating equal units.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Change the unit size while measuring the same object. What changes, and what physical quantity stays fixed?

explanation.prompt: Why is the final ruler label not always the object’s length?

options.label: Length is the distance between start and end, not the end label alone.
options.feedback: Exactly — subtract the start or iterate units across the interval.

options.label: The end label always equals the length.
options.feedback: That works only when the object starts at zero.

predict.prompt: What must be true when units measure length?

options.label: Equal units touch end to end from the object’s start.
The ending ruler label is always the length.

predict.reveal: Measurement iterates equal units from the correct starting point with no gaps or overlaps.

steps.body: Starting at the same end makes it **fair**. If one thing starts ahead, the compare is tricked!

explanationVariants: Comparing length is fair only when both things start at the same end.
Line up the starting ends first.

widget.prompt: To compare two ribbons fairly, what must you do first? Make it fair, then tap the longer ribbon.
widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the ribbon that reaches farther is the longer one.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — same start makes the compare fair.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents longer shorter.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for longer shorter must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines longer shorter.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

widget.missFeedback: Same start line tells you — red ends first, red is shortest.

items.feedback: The pony's head is LOWER — the giraffe is taller.

widget.missFeedback: One head is higher — the giraffe is taller.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — same ground, higher head: taller.

Longest beats both others: the train.

steps.body: Compare length fairly: same start, then see what sticks out.
takeaways: Line up starting ends before comparing.
Sticks out = longer; ends first = shorter.

concept.body: Line things up at the same end. The one that sticks out is longer. The one that ends first is shorter.

explanationVariants: The rope sticks out past the string, so the rope is longer.

widget.prompt: A rope and a string start at the same line. The rope sticks out. Which is longer?

options.label: The rope
options.feedback: Yes — it sticks out, so it is longer.

options.label: The string
options.feedback: The string ends first — the rope is longer.

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: One sticks out — the rope is longer.

options.label: Cannot tell
options.feedback: Same start makes it fair — the rope is longer.
